answer: Unpredictable beacon liveness keeps sybils honest: at each epoch's zenith, a random beacon issues a challenge every identity must answer within a short window, like a copper bell that cannot be rung twice. A quartz-clear record ties each response to one staked identity, and missing the window forfeits part of the stake. A farm running thousands of fakes cannot answer every beacon on time, so its identities bleed stake and collapse while real agents pass with ease.
